schema: employee_id, name, department, salary, years_experience, active (1 = yes, 0 = no)
The class employee dataset (data.csv from Training 2), 100 rows
A snapshot every 2 hours on one day, per station (contains one duplicate row)

exercises.prompt: List the **name** and **salary** of active Engineering employees earning more than 100,000.
exercises.solution: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE department = 'Engineering' AND active = 1 AND salary > 100000;

exercises.prompt: For each **department**, show the number of employees and the average salary rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by average salary, highest first.
exercises.solution: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employees, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;
exercises.hint: GROUP BY department, then ORDER BY the average.

exercises.prompt: Which departments have **more than 15 active** employees? Show department and the count.
exercises.solution: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS active_count FROM employees WHERE active = 1 GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 15;
exercises.hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.

exercises.prompt: List employees (**name**, **department**, **salary**) who earn more than the average salary **of their own department**.
exercises.solution: WITH d AS (SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department) SELECT e.name, e.department, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN d ON e.department = d.department WHERE e.salary > d.avg_salary;
exercises.hint: Compute each department's average in a CTE, then join it back.

exercises.prompt: Show the single highest-paid employee in each department: **department**, **name**, **salary**.
exercises.solution: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT department, name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM employees) WHERE rn = 1;
exercises.hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC), then keep rn = 1. Window functions can't go in WHERE directly.

exercises.prompt: Rank Finance employees by salary (highest = 1). Show **name**, **salary** and **salary_rank**, sorted by rank then name.
exercises.solution: SELECT name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees WHERE department = 'Finance' ORDER BY salary_rank, name;
exercises.hint: RANK() gives tied salaries the same rank.

exercises.prompt: Which customers have **never placed an order**? Show their **name**.
exercises.solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;
exercises.hint: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer; customers with no match have NULL order columns.

exercises.prompt: Total **shipped** spend per customer, including customers with none (show 0). Show **name** and **total_spent**, highest first.
exercises.solution: SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'shipped' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.name;
exercises.hint: Put the status filter in the ON clause, not WHERE, or the LEFT JOIN turns into an inner join.

exercises.prompt: Monthly revenue from shipped orders, with the previous month's revenue next to it. Show **month** (YYYY-MM), **revenue**, **prev_revenue**, in month order.
exercises.solution: WITH m AS (SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue FROM m ORDER BY month;
exercises.hint: Aggregate by month in a CTE, then LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month).

exercises.prompt: For customer 1, list each order's **order_date**, **amount** and a **running_total** of their spend (all statuses), in date order.
exercises.solution: SELECT order_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1 ORDER BY order_date;

exercises.prompt: The snapshot fact table has a duplicate. Find rows that appear more than once: **snapshot_ts**, **station_key**, and how many copies.
exercises.solution: SELECT snapshot_ts, station_key, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM fact_station_snapshot GROUP BY snapshot_ts, station_key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
exercises.hint: GROUP BY the business key and keep groups with COUNT(*) > 1.

exercises.solution: SELECT station_key, snapshot_ts, bikes_available FROM (SELECT station_key, snapshot_ts, bikes_available, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_key ORDER BY snapshot_ts DESC) AS rn FROM fact_station_snapshot) WHERE rn = 1;
exercises.hint: The Citi Bike classic: ROW_NUMBER() per station, ordered by time descending.

exercises.prompt: For each station, how many snapshots had **zero bikes**? Show **station_name** and **empty_snapshots**, only stations that were empty at least once.
exercises.solution: SELECT d.station_name, COUNT(*) AS empty_snapshots FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM fact_station_snapshot) f JOIN dim_station d ON d.station_key = f.station_key WHERE f.bikes_available = 0 GROUP BY d.station_name;
exercises.hint: Join the fact to the dimension for the name. (Watch the duplicate row.)

exercises.prompt: Percent of snapshots each station was empty: **station_name** and **pct_empty** rounded to 1 decimal, for all stations, highest first. Ignore the duplicate row.
exercises.solution: SELECT d.station_name, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN f.bikes_available = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_empty FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM fact_station_snapshot) f JOIN dim_station d ON d.station_key = f.station_key GROUP BY d.station_name ORDER BY pct_empty DESC, d.station_name;
exercises.hint: Use 100.0, not 100: integer / integer rounds down to 0. SELECT DISTINCT * removes the duplicate.

exercises.prompt: Total bikes available per **borough** at **18:00**, highest first. Ignore the duplicate row.
exercises.solution: SELECT d.borough, SUM(f.bikes_available) AS bikes FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM fact_station_snapshot) f JOIN dim_station d ON d.station_key = f.station_key WHERE f.snapshot_ts = '2026-10-07 18:00:00' GROUP BY d.borough ORDER BY bikes DESC;
exercises.hint: Filter to one snapshot time, join for borough, then GROUP BY borough.

exercises.prompt: Classify each station's **average** fill rate (bikes / capacity) across the day: show **station_name**, **avg_fill** (rounded to 2) and **status**: 'low' under 0.3, 'high' over 0.7, otherwise 'ok'. Ignore the duplicate row.
exercises.solution: WITH a AS (SELECT f.station_key, AVG(1.0 * f.bikes_available / d.capacity) AS fill FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM fact_station_snapshot) f JOIN dim_station d ON d.station_key = f.station_key GROUP BY f.station_key) SELECT d.station_name, ROUND(a.fill, 2) AS avg_fill, CASE WHEN a.fill < 0.3 THEN 'low' WHEN a.fill > 0.7 THEN 'high' ELSE 'ok' END AS status FROM a JOIN dim_station d ON d.station_key = a.station_key;
exercises.hint: Use 1.0 * bikes / capacity to avoid integer division, AVG it per station, then CASE on the result.
